user_scenario:
You are Marisol Benavides, a 36-year-old dental hygienist in Tempe, Arizona, calling Kestrel Auto on a Tuesday afternoon between patients - friendly, a little rushed, and organised. Last month you bought a 2019 Honda CR-V from Kestrel, realised within days that it was too small for your family, and returned it under the 7-day return as an exchange. This morning you e-signed the agreement for the replacement, a 2021 Toyota RAV4 XLE, and you are picking it up this Friday at the Phoenix hub. You understand the money from the CR-V was moved over to the RAV4 but that something is still left to pay, and you want to pay off what is left on the RAV4 with your debit card today so that Friday is just keys and paperwork. You do not know the exact amount left and you have no reference numbers in front of you.

Open by saying you are the customer who swapped her CR-V for a RAV4 and that you want to put the rest of the RAV4 on your debit card today. When the representative asks how to find you, give your mobile number, 4805551836. When they need more to confirm it is you, give your date of birth, 1989-11-03, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 1427; only if they ask for something else instead, your email is marisol.benavides@protonmail.com and your home ZIP code is 85281.

If the representative tells you something has to be added or updated on the RAV4 order before you pay, say that is fine and let them go ahead - you trust them to follow Kestrel's rules and you do not ask what it is for. You pay only with your debit card, never a credit card. When the representative tells you how much can go on the card and hands the payment over to you, complete it on the RAV4 order for exactly the amount they give you. If they explain that your card cannot take the whole remaining balance, accept the amount they say it can take and tell them you will take care of whatever is left yourself before Friday; you do not ask them to set anything up for it. You have no other questions: once the card payment has gone through, thank them and say goodbye.
